samples.summary: New slides walk early-returns on an absent/non-object element `data`, so a text element with no `data` is persisted in the exact shape that crashes every viewer
samples.evidence: `assertValidElementData` line 617: `const data = e.data as ...; if (!data || typeof data !== 'object') return;`. A payload element `{ id:'e1', type:'text', frame:{} }` therefore passes `assertValidElement` and reaches `writeSlidesRoot`, which stores it verbatim. Readers dereference unconditionally: `drawText` → `isTextBodyEmpty(data)` → `isBlocksEmpty(data.blocks)` → `blocks.length` (packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:653) throws on undefined; `migrateElement` (packages/slides/src/model/migrate.ts:156) bails for anything that is not a shape, so nothing repairs it on read. This is the same failure mode the new `assertValidTextBodyBlocks`/`normalizeSlideInlines` repair path exists to prevent (it fills `blocks`/`inlines`/`style` in), just reached one level higher. The same early return also means `data: []` (an array is `typeof 'object'`) gets the repair written as an array expando (`[].blocks = []`) that is dropped on JSON serialization, so the 'repaired' body is not what gets stored.

samples.summary: Slide table cells with an absent or non-object `body` skip validation and persist a shape every table reader dereferences
samples.evidence: `assertValidElementData` table branch: `const body = (cells[c] as { body?: unknown })?.body; if (body === undefined || body === null) continue;` — a cell of `{}` (or `null`) is accepted and stored. Consumers read it unconditionally: `packages/slides/src/view/canvas/table-renderer.ts:229 isBlocksEmpty(cell.body.blocks)`, `packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:7152 cell.body.blocks.length`, `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/table.ts:104 textBodyToXml(cell.body, …)`, `packages/slides/src/export/pdf.ts:241 bodies.push(cell.body)`. The walk repairs an absent `blocks` inside a present `body` but not the absent `body` itself, leaving the same crash class open.

samples.summary: Docs arm accepts an array as a block `style` (and as an inline `style`) while the slides arm explicitly rejects it — the block then silently loses all styling
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlock` line 371 checks only `!b.style || typeof b.style !== 'object'`, so `style: []` passes (`typeof [] === 'object'`); `assertValidBlockStyle` then reads `style.alignment`/`style[field]` off the array, all `undefined`, and passes. `serializeBlockStyleAttrs` emits `{}` for it, so the caller's block is stored with no style at all instead of getting a 400. The slides arm added the missing check (`typeof block.style !== 'object' || Array.isArray(block.style)` at line 715) but the docs arm was not updated to match. Same for `inline.style` at lines 437 and 802, where neither arm rejects an array.

samples.summary: `Number('')` is 0, so an empty attribute string reads back as a finite 0 rather than the block default — a stored `lineHeight: ''` becomes `lineHeight: 0`
samples.evidence: `parseBlockStyleAttrs` accepts any `Number.isFinite(Number(attrs[field]))`; `Number('') === 0`, so an empty-string attribute yields 0 rather than falling back to `DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE` (the backend spec even asserts this for `marginLeft`). For `lineHeight` a 0 is not a usable layout value (zero-height lines), and `parseMarginFromEdgeAttr('')` likewise returns 0 where the previous code (`attrs.marginFromEdge ? Number(...) : DEFAULT`) treated an empty attribute as absent and used `DEFAULT_HEADER_MARGIN_FROM_EDGE`. The PUT validator has the same hole: it only requires `Number.isFinite`, so `lineHeight: 0` or a negative `lineHeight`/`marginTop` reaches the layout engine.

samples.summary: `applyBlockStyle` still merges via `styleByPath`, but the new serializer can omit a key, so a cleared/non-finite style field leaves the stale CRDT value while the cache holds the new one
samples.evidence: `const merged = normalizeBlockStyle({ ...block.style, ...style }); const attrs = serializeBlockStyle(merged); … tree.styleByPath(blockPath, attrs);` — `normalizeBlockStyle` is a bare spread, so an explicitly-`undefined` key in `style` overwrites the default with `undefined`, and `serializeBlockStyleAttrs` now *omits* that attribute instead of writing it. Since `styleByPath` only merges, the previous attribute survives on the Tree node while the write-through cache is set to `merged` (line 1522) — the editor shows one value and a reload shows another. Unlike the inline path (`removedInlineStyleAttrs` + `removeStyleByPath`) and the cell path (`removedCellStyleAttrs` + `removeNodeStyle`), the block-style path has no removal counterpart. Same for `writeStylesAndRematerialize` (line 2614).

samples.summary: Group-child validation recurses with no depth bound, so a deeply nested payload throws RangeError inside the validator and surfaces as a 500 rather than a 400
samples.evidence: `assertValidElementData` group branch calls `assertValidNestedElement(children[i], …)` which calls back into `assertValidElementData`; nothing caps depth. A body with a few thousand nested `{ type:'group', data:{ children:[…] } }` levels blows the stack before any BadRequestException is thrown — the same 500-instead-of-400 outcome the whole guard exists to prevent. (The docs arm's block→table→cell→block recursion has the same property, pre-existing.)

verdict.reason: The quoted evidence checks out. assertValidElementData (docs-content.controller.ts:616-617) early-returns when `data` is absent or non-object, while assertValidElement (:560-581) only requires id/type/frame — so a text element with no `data` is accepted and written verbatim by writeSlidesRoot (slides-tree.ts:93-110). No read-side repair exists: readSlidesRoot (slides-tree.ts:52-81) unwraps only, and migrateElement (slides/src/model/migrate.ts:155-156) returns non-shape elements untouched. An unguarded consumer is reachable: `wafflebase slides export` passes the raw GET body straight to exportPptx (cli/src/commands/slides.ts:201-208, cli/src/slides/pptx-export.ts:18), reaching textElementToXml which destructures `const { data } = el` and immediately reads `data.fill` / `data.blocks` (slides/src/export/pptx/shape.ts:234-248) — TypeError on undefined; pdf.ts:236/205 and element.ts:640 are likewise unguarded. I did find one partial counterexample — the frontend Yorkie store defends itself with `(el.data ?? {})` and `blocks ?? []` (yorkie-slides-store.ts:493-511) — so the reviewer's "every viewer" is overstated, but that guard does not cover the export/raw-JSON consumers, so the defect stands. The `data: []` sub-claim also holds: an array is truthy and typeof 'object', so assertValidTextBodyBlocks writes `blocks = []` as an Array expando (:679-683) that JSON serialization drops, meaning the repair is neither stored nor echoed.

finding.summary: New slide text-body walk accepts a text body with `blocks` absent, which is a TypeError in every renderer of the stored deck
finding.evidence: `assertValidTextBodyBlocks` early-returns when `blocks === undefined || blocks === null` (line 671), so `PUT` bodies like `{id:'e1',type:'text',frame:{},data:{}}` or `{type:'shape',data:{text:{}}}` pass validation and are persisted verbatim by `writeSlidesRoot`. On read, `isTextBodyEmpty(body)` → `isBlocksEmpty(body.blocks)` does `blocks.length === 0` (packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:653) and `migrateElement` (packages/slides/src/model/migrate.ts:155) does NOT backfill `data.blocks` — only shape fill/stroke are migrated. So `blocks` undefined throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')` for every viewer of the deck. This is exactly the failure mode `normalizeSlideInlines` was added to prevent for `inlines`; the same repair (`body.blocks = []`) is not applied here.

verdict.reason: The finding's central claim is not present in the code. It asserts `assertValidTextBodyBlocks` "early-returns" on absent `blocks` and that "the same repair (`body.blocks = []`) is not applied here". The actual function (docs-content.controller.ts:675-690) does exactly the opposite: when `blocks === undefined || blocks === null` it assigns `body.blocks = []` before returning, mirroring `normalizeSlideInlines` (772-780) and the `block.style = {}` / `inline.style = {}` fill-ins (713, 799). The cited "line 671" is a line of the doc comment (664-673) that explicitly documents this fill-in, not an early return. Both named payloads are repaired: `{type:'text',data:{}}` via assertValidElementData (618-619), and `{type:'shape',data:{text:{}}}` via assertValidTextBody (644-651). The mutation reaches persistence because assertValidSlidesBody(body) at line 153 mutates the same object passed to writeSlidesRoot(root, body) at line 193 and echoed at 198, so no deck can be stored with `blocks` absent and the downstream isBlocksEmpty/migrateElement TypeError path is never reached from this endpoint.

finding.summary: Slide block with no `style` is accepted, but the PPTX exporter dereferences `block.style` unconditionally
finding.evidence: `assertValidSlideBlocks` only validates `style` when it is present (`if (block.style !== undefined && block.style !== null)`, line 694) — deliberately, per the doc comment. But `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:99` does `ALGN.get(block.style.alignment)` and lines 105/107/113/119/122 read `block.style.marginLeft/textIndent/lineHeight/marginTop/marginBottom` with no guard, so a stored block without `style` throws during PPTX export of that deck. The canvas path survives only because `text-renderer.ts` normalizes styles first; the export path does not. Same class as the `inlines` repair — either repair `block.style = {}` or reject.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `assertValidSlideBlocks` only checks `style` when present and never repairs it, leaving `blockToXml`'s unconditional `block.style.alignment` deref exposed. The exporter deref is real (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:99,105,107,113,119,122), but the guard said to be missing is present in the very function named: packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:706-713 does `if (block.style === undefined || block.style === null) { block.style = {}; }` — exactly the "repair block.style = {}" remedy requested, with a comment citing `ALGN.get(block.style.alignment)` as the reason. The quoted condition "line 694 `if (block.style !== undefined && block.style !== null)`" is not in the tree (line 694 is doc-comment text). The repair reaches persistence: `block` is the live parsed payload object, validation runs at putContent:153 before `writeSlidesRoot(root, body)` at :193 on that same object, so `{}` is what gets stored and later exported. Every slide-block path routes through this guard: text bodies via assertValidElementData:619/650 -> assertValidTextBodyBlocks:689 -> assertValidSlideBlocks (covering text, shape.data.text, table cell bodies, and group children via assertValidNestedElement:595-599), and slide notes via :557.
